symptom: `mxcli run restart` refusing a run started with a literal --db-password said to set the database password in PGPASSWORD; a run started that way connected to PostgreSQL with the default password `mendix`.
cause: PGPASSWORD is read only by the psql calls of --ensure-db (ensuredb.go, localapp.go). The runtime's DatabasePassword comes from --db-password and defaults to `mendix` (localapp.go), so the hint named a variable nothing on that path reads.
insight: A remedy in an error message is a claim about another code path, and it was never tried: grep for who reads the variable before naming it. The working remedy needed a value restart can re-resolve, which is the @env:/@file: reference --constant already had (#1769); giving the secret flags the same resolver made restart work instead of only rewording the refusal. The test asserts the refusal names @env: and not PGPASSWORD; redaction and detach tests fail with isValueReference or the flag-value guard stubbed.
